newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU clears bids to export 142,000 T wheat to Africa.
newsitem.headline: EU clears bids to export 142,000 T wheat to Africa.

text.p: The European Union has accepted bids from grain firms to export 142,000 tonnes of soft wheat to a target group of African nations under a system of short-term licences, France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday.
Exporters bid for the licences, which carry a rebate of 28 Ecus per tonne, last Friday through France.
The licences, valid for the current month plus four months, give preferential terms to the EU's traditional African clients.
Grain firms also applied through France under the same scheme on Monday and Tuesday to export an additional 4,500 tonnes of wheat to Africa,
The European Commission has until Thursday to decide whether to accept or reject these additional requests.
Last Friday exporters also bid through France to export up to 800,000 tonnes of soft wheat under longer licences valid until June 30, 1997.
Under this scheme, they must show proof of contracts to receive the same rebate of 28 Ecus per tonne.
ONIC officials said that under the so-called Article Nine rule, when the EU clears applications for long-term export licences it sets a deadline for exporters to show the contracts.
It was not immediately clear when the EU planned to review these applications, but one industry source said that might come up for discussion at this week's EU grain committee meeting.
